title: A parallel line through a point
statement: Make a line that is parallel to y = 2x + 1 and passes through the point (3, 4).
goal: Student writes y = 2x - 2 (or y - 4 = 2(x - 3)) and explains that parallel lines share a slope, so the slope is 2, and the intercept comes from making (3, 4) satisfy the equation.
common_misconceptions: Using the negative reciprocal slope (-1/2), which gives a perpendicular line
Keeping the intercept 1 as well as the slope, so the line is the same as the original
Swapping x and y when substituting the point: 3 = 2(4) + b
Thinking parallel lines must have the same y-intercept
hint_ladder: Ask what 'parallel' means for two lines on the graph, and what feature of the equation controls steepness.
Ask which number in y = 2x + 1 is the slope and whether a parallel line can have a different one.
Plot the point (3, 4) as a tutor point and ask whether their line goes through it.
Suggest a slider b in y = 2x + b and ask which b puts the line through (3, 4).
Ask them to substitute x = 3, y = 4 into y = 2x + b and solve for b.
